note: Misses every stated criterion. He is a salaried employee in a sedentary Monday-to-Friday job, not a business owner or physician; he self-reports $65,000-$70,000 a year against ongoing hospital bills and about $600 in the bank, so 'makes good money' fails on both nominal income and liquidity. Health is not the neglected corner of an otherwise good life, it is the crisis at the centre of it — a diabetic foot infection, an amputation and three hospital admissions inside a year. And he is the explicit exclusion in the stated ICP almost verbatim: he describes himself before September 2025 as 'total fat guy... I was drinking, eating. I wasn't doing anything', and has since lost about 85 lb. This is rescue, not good-to-great. Judged purely on the criteria as written and not on intent: his commitment and self-discipline are exceptional, which is precisely why he is worth flagging — the stated ICP would have screened out the most motivated prospect in this batch, while the clinical risk it does not screen for at all is the thing that should have stopped this sale.
